v.rationale:
Both suites pass (11 and 12 tests). I also ran throwaway probes against both implementations, then deleted them: 409/404 without an Accept header, a listener that throws on the first call followed by a retry (which returns 200 without creating a second row), and a pre-seeded redemption on an exhausted coupon (200, with integer JSON fields). Both behaved correctly.

The two designs are nearly identical and both correct for MySQL across several servers. Each locks the coupon row inside a transaction, checks for the user's existing redemption before checking the cap, has a unique (coupon_id, user_id) index as a backstop, and dispatches the event after commit only when wasRecentlyCreated is true. I found no real bugs in either.

impl-2 ranks first because it puts the 'event exactly once per new redemption' rule inside the domain method, Coupon::redeem. In impl-1 the controller has to remember to dispatch the event, so another caller of redeemFor would skip it. impl-2 also has slightly tidier exception idioms (a $message property and throw_if with a class string) and somewhat broader edge-case tests (zero capacity, exhaustion reached through real requests, factories). impl-1 does have a nice non-JSON 401 test and a clean firstOrNew. The margin is small.
